subject: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2028-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding so far — the evaluation trial looked promising. The procurement and SRE teams at Acme are collecting the final SLA specifics for our RFP packet. We need a concise response that covers:

- Uptime target(s) and how they are measured (time window, aggregation).
- Latency commitments (which percentiles, token-length assumptions, and endpoint variants).
- Exact service credit calculation and cap.
- Measurement methodology: telemetry sources, sampling, synthetic probes vs customer traffic, and evidence we can request.
- Exclusions (maintenance windows, customer misconfiguration, force majeure).

Can you provide a document and a one-page summary we can include in the RFP? Also let us know whether your platform can provide raw telemetry slices for a rolling 90-day window if requested during an audit.

Regards,
Alice Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation

P.S. We may need SOC2 audit artifacts as supporting evidence — procurement will flag it if not included.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2028-01-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise SLO spec (redwood-slo-spec-v1.pdf) and a measurement matrix spreadsheet for the RFP team. High level answers below; Monica from CS will follow up with telemetry details.

High-level SLO snapshot (proposed):
- Availability: 99.9% measured monthly per-account across the primary endpoint. Measurement: internal telemetry using production request sampling + probe corroboration.
- Latency: p95 < 150ms for payloads <= 512 tokens on the generation endpoint (regional hosted tier). p99 targets available for dedicated deployments at negotiation.
- Service credits: prorated monthly credit = (Downtime minutes / Total minutes in month) * Monthly invoice. Credit cap: 50% of monthly invoice for a single month; cumulative annual cap 200% unless otherwise agreed.

Key notes: credits are issued following evidence review (telemetry + synthetic probes). Maintenance windows announced with 72h notice are excluded. We do provide raw telemetry slices for audits under an NDA and a one-time evidence request process — Monica will detail the format.

Attaching: redwood-slo-spec-v1.pdf, measurement-matrix-2028.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Hi Alice / Karthik — adding the measurement and evidence details so procurement and SRE can validate: 

Telemetry sources and method:
- Primary signal: production request telemetry ingested by our telemetry pipeline (per-request metadata includes timestamp, region, model_id, route, client_id, token_count, latency_ms, response_code).
- Secondary signal: synthetic probes from regional collectors running once per minute (latency + success), used to corroborate availability anomalies.
- Sampling: 100% retention of error traces; adaptive sampling for successful requests (default 1 in 100) with configurable higher sampling for customers during audit windows.

Measurement windows and aggregation:
- Availability is computed on a per-account, per-region basis: uptime % = (Total successful minutes in month / Total minutes in month) * 100, where a minute is considered successful if at least one successful request is recorded for the route in that minute.
- Latency percentiles are calculated on the sampled dataset, normalized to a per-route token-bucket (we annotate percentile tables with token-size buckets: <=128, 129-512, >512). For contractual p95 guarantees we use the <=512 bucket unless otherwise negotiated.

Exclusions and dispute process:
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (72h notice), customer misconfiguration (as evidenced by request headers/keys), DDoS attacks mitigated by third-party network providers, and force majeure.
- Disputes: customer can open a claim within 30 days of incident. We provide telemetry slices, probe logs, and config snapshots. If there is disagreement, an independent third-party measurement can be requested (cost sharing negotiated).

Evidence delivery format:
- We provide CSV slices with request-level fields and a summarized PDF report for the incident. For full audits we can provide time-aligned probe logs and configuration snapshots under NDA. Typical turnaround for evidence packaging: 5-10 business days.

Let me know if you need different sampling rates, or immediate elevated retention for the RFP review period.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2028-01-11T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A couple follow-ups from our SRE and legal: 

1) The 50% monthly cap is higher than some vendors; can you confirm whether you can offer an elevated one-off credit (100% of monthly invoice) for a P1 incident lasting more than 12 continuous hours? Our leadership is pushing for stronger protections for core production workloads.

2) For latency: we need clarity on whether p95 latency guarantees apply to bursty request patterns under sustained concurrent ramp (e.g., 2k rps sustained for 10 minutes). Can you state the operational assumptions or whether this falls under "performance degradation" governed by dedicated capacity sizing?

3) SOC2: procurement flagged that we need SOC2 Type II report access. Do you provide a report or a SOC2 point of contact?

If you can put the revised SLO paragraph in a form we can drop in the RFP, that would be great.

-Alice
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Alice — looping in Aditya on the credit ask and adding a brief response to the performance question below. Proposed compromise below that should be acceptable for most enterprise agreements: 

1) Service credit escalation for P1 (continuous outage > 12 hours): we can offer a one-time elevated credit equal to 100% of the monthly invoice for that billing month, subject to post-incident evidence review and a maximum single-incident cap of 100% (i.e., we would not exceed 100%). Annual cumulative cap remains 200% unless we agree otherwise in enterprise addendum.

2) Latency and burst assumptions: our hosted tier p95 guarantee assumes a typical mixed workload with reasonable burst headroom; it is not sized for sustained 2k rps for 10 minutes on the shared hosted offering. For sustained high-concurrency workloads we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) where we provide negotiated p95/p99 guarantees with defined concurrency and sequence-length bounds. We will include a short clause for the RFP indicating that p95 guarantees are conditioned on workload profiles documented in the measurement-matrix.

Aditya — can you confirm approval to include the P1 escalation credit language and the single-incident 100% cap in the RFP paragraph?

Best,
Karthik
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T15:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Inference platform SLA details and measurement methodology

Karthik/Monica/Alice — approved. We will include the following RFP-ready paragraph and provide the amended PDF: 

"Availability and credits: Redwood Inference guarantees 99.9% monthly availability for the primary hosted inference endpoint (measured per-account, per-region). Standard service credit calculation is prorated by minute: (Downtime minutes / Total minutes in month) * Monthly invoice. Standard credit cap for a single month is 50% of the monthly invoice. For a P1 incident defined as a continuous outage >12 hours, Redwood will offer a one-time elevated credit equal to 100% of the monthly invoice for that month, subject to evidence review. Cumulative annual credit cap is 200% of monthly fees unless otherwise agreed in an enterprise addendum. Exclusions include scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, customer misconfiguration, DDoS events mitigated by third parties, and force majeure. Evidence and telemetry slices will be provided under NDA within 5-10 business days of a validated incident."

We will attach the updated redwood-slo-spec-v1.1.pdf and a one-page RFP paragraph for you to insert. Monica will prepare the evidence checklist and SOC2 contact details (we can provide our SOC2 Type II report under an NDA).

Regards,
Aditya Rao
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
